backendRemediationsMerged.note: A keyset cursor minted from a JS Date loses a timestamptz column's microseconds, so the descending predicate skips every row sharing the boundary's millisecond — silently, and guaranteed rather than raced wherever one transaction writes a batch. Measured: 10 rows at one instant, limit=4, page 2 returned 0 of the remaining 6. Fixed at 9 sites; 16 pre-existing sites are listed with file and line in docs/phase-1/phase-1-27/findings/p1-27-int-006-cursor-precision.md. Found by an adversarial review workflow — 13 candidates, 9 refuted, 4 survived — and then verified independently against the live database before any code changed.

openFindings.subject: The web API client defaults Idempotency-Key on POST only, so every NON-POST operation marked idempotent answers 400 ERR-INT-002 before permissions are even evaluated
openFindings.disposition: P1-27 work — apps/web, so it belongs in the feature branch
openFindings.correctedScope: Recorded originally as affecting PUT. Counted against the register it is NINE operations, not six: PUT crm.preference-set, crm.customer-status-set, dia.diagnostic-item-result, qms.qc-check-result, qms.rework-cost-record, wo.additional-work-detail-record — AND PATCH veh.vehicle-update, veh.vehicle-status-change, svc.service-update. apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts states in its own docblock that 'PATCH and DELETE are not marked idempotent anywhere in the published contract', which is false and is the sentence that would stop the next reader checking. veh.vehicle-update is PATCH /vehicles/{vehicleId} — the edit path behind FE-019.
